title: feat(rules): Review PyTorch DataLoader with num_workers > 0 lacking worker_init_fn (R116)
body:
### Context & Motivation
In PyTorch, when creating a `DataLoader` with `num_workers > 0`, each subprocess worker inherits the same NumPy and Python random state as the parent process unless a custom `worker_init_fn` is provided. This is a notorious source of subtle reproducibility failures in deep learning (documented in the [PyTorch Reproducibility Guide](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/randomness.html#dataloader)). Each worker ends up generating identical random augmentations or permutations across processes.

### Proposed Specification
Introduce rule **R116** (`review` level):
Flag calls to `torch.utils.data.DataLoader` (and imported `DataLoader`) where:
1. `num_workers` is passed as a positive integer literal (`> 0`) or variable, AND
2. `worker_init_fn` is missing or explicitly `None`.

### Passing and Failing Examples
```python
# ❌ FAILS (R116 review): num_workers > 0 without worker_init_fn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=32, num_workers=4, shuffle=True)

# ❌ FAILS (R116 review): explicit worker_init_fn=None
loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=32, num_workers=2, worker_init_fn=None)

# ✅ PASSES: worker_init_fn provided
def seed_worker(worker_id):
    worker_seed = torch.initial_seed() % 2**32
    np.random.seed(worker_seed)
    random.seed(worker_seed)

g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(42)
loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=32, num_workers=4, worker_init_fn=seed_worker, generator=g)

# ✅ PASSES: single process (num_workers=0 or omitted)
loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=32, generator=g)
```

### Implementation Pointers
- `src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`: Add `DataLoader` check in PyTorch inspection functions.
- `src/repro_lens/analysis.py`: Register rule code `R116` in `RULES`.
- `tests/test_frameworks.py`: Add positive and negative test cases.
- `docs/rules.md` & `docs/frameworks.md`: Document rule definition and limitations.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rule R116 implemented with stdlib AST only.
- [ ] Unit tests covering missing vs present `worker_init_fn`.
- [ ] Zero false alarms on `num_workers=0` or omitted `num_workers`.
- [ ] Documentation updated in `docs/rules.md`.

title: feat(rules): Hugging Face Transformers TrainingArguments / Trainer determinism check (R117)
body:
### Context & Motivation
Hugging Face `transformers` is the standard library for NLP and LLM training. `TrainingArguments` provides `seed`, `data_seed`, and `full_determinism`. By default:
- `full_determinism` is `False`.
- `data_seed` defaults to `None`.
Without `full_determinism=True`, PyTorch deterministic algorithms and worker seeds are not fully locked down, leading to run-to-run variations in evaluations.

### Proposed Specification
Introduce rule **R117** (`review` level):
1. Target calls to `transformers.TrainingArguments(...)` or `TrainingArguments(...)`.
2. Report R117 if `full_determinism` is not explicitly set to `True`, or if `data_seed` is missing when dataset preprocessing/shuffling occurs.

### Passing and Failing Examples
```python
# ❌ FAILS (R117 review): default arguments omit full_determinism
from transformers import TrainingArguments

args = TrainingArguments(output_dir="./results", per_device_train_batch_size=16)

# ✅ PASSES: explicit full_determinism and seeds specified
args = TrainingArguments(
    output_dir="./results",
    seed=42,
    data_seed=42,
    full_determinism=True,
)
```

### Implementation Pointers
- `src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`: Add `TRANSFORMERS` argument inspection helper using `Arguments.call`.
- `docs/frameworks.md`: Add a new section for Hugging Face Transformers.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AST parsing for `transformers.TrainingArguments` and `Trainer`.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/test_frameworks.py`.
- [ ] Passing documentation in `docs/frameworks.md`.

title: feat(rules): Detect Polars DataFrame random sampling without seed (R118)
body:
### Context & Motivation
Following the implementation of `R115` for `pandas.DataFrame.sample()`, Polars is increasingly replacing Pandas in high-performance ML pipelines. Calling `DataFrame.sample()` or `LazyFrame.sample()` without the `seed` keyword argument draws non-deterministic random subsamples on every execution.

### Proposed Specification
Introduce rule **R118** (`review` level):
Flag `.sample(...)` method calls on variables or chains where:
- The `seed` keyword argument is missing or set to `None`.

### Passing and Failing Examples
```python
# ❌ FAILS (R118 review): unseeded sample
import polars as pl
df = pl.read_csv("data.csv")
sample = df.sample(n=100)

# ✅ PASSES: explicit seed passed
sample = df.sample(n=100, seed=42)
sample = df.sample(fraction=0.2, seed=123)
```

### Implementation Pointers
- Model directly after `R115` (`src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`).
- Add tests in `tests/test_frameworks.py`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Detects unseeded `.sample(n=...)` and `.sample(fraction=...)`.
- [ ] Honors `# repro-lens: ignore[R118]`.
- [ ] Full unit test coverage.

title: feat(rules): Detect unseeded CatBoostClassifier / CatBoostRegressor (R119)
body:
### Context & Motivation
CatBoost is one of the three major gradient boosting libraries alongside XGBoost (`R104`) and LightGBM (`R105`). While CatBoost has a default `random_seed=0`, initializing estimators without explicitly specifying `random_seed` often leads to issues when tuning hyperparameters or parallelizing training across multi-threaded workers.

### Proposed Specification
Introduce rule **R119** (`review` level):
Flag `CatBoostClassifier`, `CatBoostRegressor`, and `CatBoost` when initialized without explicit `random_seed` (or alias `random_state`).

### Passing and Failing Examples
```python
# ❌ FAILS (R119 review): no explicit random_seed
from catboost import CatBoostClassifier
model = CatBoostClassifier(iterations=100)

# ✅ PASSES: explicit random_seed
model = CatBoostClassifier(iterations=100, random_seed=42)
```

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Inspect calls to `catboost.CatBoostClassifier`, `CatBoostRegressor`, `CatBoost`.
- [ ] Handle parameter dictionary expansion.
- [ ] Add tests in `tests/test_frameworks.py`.

title: feat(rules): Review CUDA determinism without CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG set (R120)
body:
### Context & Motivation
In PyTorch, running `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` on CUDA >= 10.2 will throw a runtime error (`RuntimeError: Deterministic behavior was requested, but CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG was not set`) unless the environment variable `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` or `:16:8` is configured before CUDA initialization.

### Proposed Specification
Introduce rule **R120** (`review` level):
In any file where `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` is invoked, check if `os.environ["CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG"]` (or `os.putenv`) is assigned in the file. If absent, emit R120 advising the developer to set the environment variable.

### Passing and Failing Examples
```python
# ❌ FAILS (R120 review): deterministic algorithms enabled without setting CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG
import torch
torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)

# ✅ PASSES: environment variable set prior to call
import os
import torch
os.environ["CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG"] = ":4096:8"
torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
```

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rule R120 implemented in `src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`.
- [ ] Documented in `docs/frameworks.md` with links to official PyTorch docs.

title: feat(cli): Add baseline file support (--write-baseline / --baseline) for gradual adoption
body:
### Context & Motivation
Similar to `mypy --shadow-file`, `detekt --baseline`, or `flake8` baseline plugins: when a team introduces ReproLens into an existing large ML codebase, hundreds of legacy warnings can block CI adoption. Teams need a way to record current findings in a `.repro-lens-baseline.json` file so that only **new** regressions fail the build.

### Proposed Specification
1. Add `repro-lens check --write-baseline [PATH]`:
   - Runs scan and writes a JSON snapshot of finding signatures (`file_path`, `rule_code`, hashed call context or line/col).
2. Add `repro-lens check --baseline [PATH]`:
   - Filters out any finding present in the baseline file.
   - Emits an exit code of `0` if all detected findings are in the baseline.
   - Reports newly introduced findings with standard exit code.
   - Warns if baseline entries no longer match any code (optional `--clean-baseline`).

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--write-baseline <path>` generates portable baseline JSON.
- [ ] `--baseline <path>` suppresses recorded findings.
- [ ] Tested in `tests/test_project.py` with mock repos.
- [ ] Documentation added to `docs/quickstart.md`.

title: feat(cli): Add rich terminal output mode (--format pretty) with code underlines
body:
### Context & Motivation
Currently, `repro-lens check --format text` prints simple line messages:
`src/train.py:12:1 R101 [warning] train_test_split lacks explicit random_state`
Modern developer tools like Ruff, Cargo, and Biome display clear snippets with line numbers, code excerpts, and caret (`^^^^`) underlines highlighting the exact error.

### Proposed Specification
Add `--format pretty` (and make it default when `sys.stdout.isatty()` is True):
```text
warning[R101]: A supported randomized sklearn call lacks explicit non-None random_state
  --> src/train.py:12:1
   |
12 | X_train, X_test = train_test_split(X, y)
   |                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ missing explicit random_state
   |
   = help: Pass an explicit seed, e.g. train_test_split(..., random_state=42)
```
- Must remain **stdlib-only** (use standard ANSI escapes; no Rich or external dependencies).

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ANSI syntax formatting implemented in stdlib.
- [ ] Clean fallback when `NO_COLOR` is set or stdout is piped.
- [ ] Tests verifying output formatting.

title: feat(config): Support per-rule severity overrides and rule ignore lists in pyproject.toml
body:
### Context & Motivation
Currently, users cannot adjust severities (e.g. promoting `R105` review to `warning`, or demoting `R101` warning to `review`), nor can they ignore specific rules globally across a project without adding inline comments to every file.

### Proposed Specification
Extend `[tool.repro-lens]` configuration in `pyproject.toml`:
```toml
[tool.repro-lens]
ignore = ["R104", "R108"]

[tool.repro-lens.severities]
R105 = "warning"
R106 = "error"
```
1. `ignore`: List of rule IDs that will be completely skipped during analysis.
2. `severities`: Map of `RULE_ID = "warning" | "review" | "error"` to override defaults.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Parsed in `src/repro_lens/project.py:read_policy`.
- [ ] Validated against known rule codes.
- [ ] Unit tests verifying overrides in `tests/test_project.py`.

title: feat(cli): Add --diff / --suggest mode for automated random_state suggestions
body:
### Context & Motivation
ReproLens flags missing seeds like `train_test_split(X, y)` or `RandomForestClassifier()`. Contributors and developers frequently ask for autofix suggestions or a unified diff showing how to fix the finding with an explicit seed.

### Proposed Specification
Add a `--diff` flag to `repro-lens check`:
- Computes unified diff showing suggested insertions (e.g. adding `random_state=42` or `# repro-lens: ignore[R101] -- Reason`).
- Does not edit files in-place unless `--fix` is passed.
- Uses Python stdlib `difflib`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CLI argument `--diff` prints unified diff to stdout.
- [ ] Preserves indentation and existing arguments.
- [ ] Unit tests for multi-line and single-line call sites.

title: feat(verify): Support numeric tolerance (epsilon / abs_tol / rel_tol) in verify and compare
body:
### Context & Motivation
Deep learning models and multi-threaded CPU libraries frequently yield minute numerical variations (e.g. 0.945000001 vs 0.945000000) due to floating-point associativity and non-deterministic atomic operations on GPUs. Currently, `repro-lens verify` and `repro-lens compare` check exact equality of metric values in `result.json`.

### Proposed Specification
1. In `pyproject.toml`:
   ```toml
   [tool.repro-lens.verify]
   abs-tol = 1e-5
   rel-tol = 1e-4
   ```
2. In `repro-lens compare report1.json report2.json --abs-tol 1e-5`:
   - Use `math.isclose(a, b, rel_tol=..., abs_tol=...)` for numeric metric comparisons.
   - If values differ within tolerance, report as `matched (within tolerance)`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tolerant comparison implemented in `src/repro_lens/comparison.py`.
- [ ] Configurable via `pyproject.toml` and CLI flag.
- [ ] Tests covering floating point comparisons.

title: feat(verify): Capture hardware & runtime fingerprint (CPU, GPU, CUDA, OS) in verification reports
body:
### Context & Motivation
When comparing experiment runs using `repro-lens compare`, outputs may diverge simply because run A ran on an Intel CPU and run B ran on an Apple Silicon or NVIDIA GPU. Recording hardware metadata provides immediate evidence of environmental discrepancies.

### Proposed Specification
Extend `verify()` output schema in `result.json` to include an `environment` block:
```json
"environment": {
  "platform": "Darwin-23.5.0-arm64",
  "python": "3.11.8",
  "processor": "arm",
  "cuda_available": false
}
```
All details must be collected using standard library modules (`platform`, `sys`, `os`).

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Environment block added to verify report.
- [ ] `compare` highlights environment differences if metrics mismatch.
- [ ] Unit tests in `tests/test_verify.py`.

title: feat(init): Add a reproducible PyTorch & Lightning template to repro-lens init

title: perf(analysis): Implement parallel multi-process scanning for large codebases
body:
### Context & Motivation
In large machine learning repositories containing hundreds of notebooks and scripts, scanning files sequentially in a single thread can take several seconds.

### Proposed Specification
In `src/repro_lens/project.py`:
- Use `concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor` to analyze files in parallel when file count exceeds a threshold (e.g. > 20 files).
- Maintain deterministic output ordering by collecting results and sorting by `(path, cell, line, code)`.
- Support `--jobs / -j` CLI flag to control worker concurrency.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Parallel AST analysis using stdlib `concurrent.futures`.
- [ ] Benchmarks showing >= 2x speedup on multi-core machines for large projects.
- [ ] Deterministic sorting preserved.

title: feat(rules): Detect unseeded DistributedSampler & missing set_epoch() in PyTorch DDP (R121)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: PyTorch DistributedDataParallel (DDP) & Hugging Face Accelerate.
- **Problem**: When using `DistributedSampler` in PyTorch DDP:
  1. If `seed` is not passed, it defaults to `0`, which is fine, but if workers randomize it independently, worker batches overlap.
  2. More critically: if `sampler.set_epoch(epoch)` is omitted at the beginning of each epoch in the training loop, the sampler yields the exact same shuffle order for *every single epoch*! This is documented in the [PyTorch DDP tutorial](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html#torch.utils.data.distributed.DistributedSampler) as one of the most common silent bugs in distributed training.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Rule `R121` (`review` level):
    1. Flag `DistributedSampler(dataset)` when `seed` keyword is missing or `shuffle=True` without seed control.
    2. Check `for epoch in ...:` loops containing `for ... in dataloader:` to verify if `sampler.set_epoch` is invoked. If absent, emit a warning.
- **Example**:
  ```python
  # ❌ FAILS (R121 review): sampler.set_epoch(epoch) missing inside epoch loop
  sampler = DistributedSampler(dataset)
  loader = DataLoader(dataset, sampler=sampler)
  for epoch in range(epochs):
      for batch in loader:
          train_step(batch)

  # ✅ PASSES:
  for epoch in range(epochs):
      sampler.set_epoch(epoch)
      for batch in loader:
          train_step(batch)
  ```
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`, `tests/test_frameworks.py`.

---

title: feat(rules): Detect stale / un-split JAX PRNG keys (R122)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: JAX / Flax functional PRNG design.
- **Problem**: JAX has explicit stateless PRNGs (`jax.random.PRNGKey`). A classic JAX anti-pattern is reusing the same PRNG key across multiple stochastic calls (e.g. `jax.random.normal(key, ...)`) instead of splitting it (`key, subkey = jax.random.split(key)`). Reusing the same key produces identical numbers in different layers or steps!
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Rule `R122` (`warning` level):
    - Track AST variable names assigned from `jax.random.PRNGKey` or `jax.random.split`.
    - If the same key variable is passed into multiple `jax.random.*` calls in the same function scope without a re-splitting statement, flag the subsequent calls.
- **Example**:
  ```python
  # ❌ FAILS (R122 warning): key reused without split
  key = jax.random.PRNGKey(42)
  w1 = jax.random.normal(key, (10, 10))
  w2 = jax.random.normal(key, (10, 10))  # w2 will be identical to w1!

  # ✅ PASSES:
  key, subkey1, subkey2 = jax.random.split(key, 3)
  w1 = jax.random.normal(subkey1, (10, 10))
  w2 = jax.random.normal(subkey2, (10, 10))
  ```
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`, `tests/test_frameworks.py`.

---

title: feat(rules): Detect unseeded Ray Train / Ray Tune distributed worker actors (R123)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: Ray Train (Anyscale) distributed training pipelines.
- **Problem**: Ray executes training functions across distributed actors/workers in separate processes. If the training function seeds with a fixed constant (e.g. `torch.manual_seed(42)`), all worker processes across the cluster generate identical random batches, corrupting parallel data loading. Each worker must combine the base seed with `ray.train.get_context().get_world_rank()`.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Rule `R123` (`review` level):
    - In functions decorated with `@ray.remote` or passed to `TorchTrainer(train_loop_per_worker=...)`, flag hardcoded fixed seeds in `torch.manual_seed(N)` or `np.random.seed(N)` if the rank/worker ID is not incorporated.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`.

---

title: feat(rules): Flag torch.cuda.manual_seed without manual_seed_all in multi-GPU code (R124)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: PyTorch multi-GPU randomness guidelines.
- **Problem**: `torch.cuda.manual_seed(seed)` only initializes the RNG for the currently active GPU (default GPU 0). If the script uses `torch.cuda.device_count() > 1`, `DataParallel`, or multi-GPU tensors, GPUs 1..N remain unseeded.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Rule `R124` (`warning` level):
    - When `torch.cuda.manual_seed(...)` is used, recommend `torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(...)` unless explicit single-GPU affinity is established.
- **Example**:
  ```python
  # ❌ FAILS:
  torch.cuda.manual_seed(42)

  # ✅ PASSES:
  torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(42)
  ```
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`.

---

title: feat(rules): Detect non-deterministic LLM generation parameters in vLLM & Hugging Face (R125)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: vLLM (`SamplingParams`), Hugging Face `GenerationConfig`, and OpenAI SDK.
- **Problem**: In Generative AI pipelines and LLM evaluation benchmarks, `SamplingParams(temperature=0.7)` or `model.generate(..., do_sample=True)` without an explicit `seed=` produces completely non-deterministic responses on each call. This invalidates LLM-as-a-judge scores and benchmark comparisons.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Rule `R125` (`warning` level):
    - Flag `vllm.SamplingParams` or `SamplingParams` where `temperature > 0` and `seed` is omitted or `None`.
    - Flag `model.generate(...)` or `GenerationConfig(...)` where `do_sample=True` and `seed` is missing.
- **Example**:
  ```python
  # ❌ FAILS:
  from vllm import SamplingParams
  params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95)

  # ✅ PASSES:
  params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95, seed=42)
  ```
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`.

---

title: feat(rules): Detect train-test data leakage via pre-split fit() / fit_transform() (R126)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: `dslinter` (Delft University of Technology) & `Cleanlab`.
- **Problem**: A catastrophic reproducibility and scientific validity issue: calling `StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)` or `imputer.fit(X)` *before* calling `train_test_split(X, y)` leaks information (mean, variance, distribution) from the test set into the training pipeline.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Rule `R126` (`warning` level):
    - Identify transformer estimators (`StandardScaler`, `MinMaxScaler`, `SimpleImputer`, `PCA`, etc.).
    - In the same scope, if `.fit()` or `.fit_transform()` is called on a dataset variable *prior* to that variable being split by `train_test_split()`, flag data leakage.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/analysis.py`.

---

title: feat(rules): Detect unseeded dataset.shuffle() in Hugging Face Datasets (R127)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: Hugging Face `datasets` library.
- **Problem**: Calling `dataset.shuffle()` in HF Datasets uses Python's global RNG or internal seeds unless `seed=` is explicitly provided. Unseeded shuffling also prevents Hugging Face's disk caching mechanism from reusing shuffled shards.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Rule `R127` (`review` level):
    - Inspect method calls `.shuffle(...)` on suspected HF dataset objects or `load_dataset(...)` chains. Flag if `seed` is missing.
- **Example**:
  ```python
  # ❌ FAILS:
  dataset = dataset.shuffle()

  # ✅ PASSES:
  dataset = dataset.shuffle(seed=42)
  ```
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`.

---

title: feat(rules): Flag order-dependent iteration over unordered sets/dicts in feature pipelines (R128)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: CPython `PYTHONHASHSEED` non-determinism.
- **Problem**: In Python 3.3+, string hash randomization is enabled by default (`PYTHONHASHSEED=random`). Iterating over a `set` (e.g. `for category in set(labels):`) or converting `list(set(x))` creates an arbitrary ordering that changes every time Python restarts! If this order is used to map categorical features to integer IDs, model inputs differ between runs.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Rule `R128` (`review` level):
    - Flag `for x in set(...)` or `list(set(...))` when used in feature encoding, vocabulary construction, or indexing logic without wrapping in `sorted(...)`.
- **Example**:
  ```python
  # ❌ FAILS (R128 review): set ordering varies across Python process restarts
  vocab = {token: idx for idx, token in enumerate(set(tokens))}

  # ✅ PASSES: deterministic sorting
  vocab = {token: idx for idx, token in enumerate(sorted(set(tokens)))}
  ```
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/analysis.py`.

---

title: feat(rules): Detect non-deterministic partition shuffling in Dask DataFrames (R129)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: Dask distributed dataframe execution.
- **Problem**: In Dask, `ddf.shuffle()` or `ddf.sample(frac=0.5)` partitions data across workers. Without specifying `shuffle="tasks"` or passing a deterministic `random_state`, partition division and sample extraction diverge between scheduler runs.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Rule `R129` (`review` level):
    - Check `dask.dataframe` calls to `.sample()` or `.shuffle()` lacking explicit `random_state` or `seed`.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`.

---

title: feat(rules): Warn on GPU operations with non-deterministic CUDA atomicAdd (R130)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: PyTorch Reproducibility Notes & NVIDIA NGC determinism docs.
- **Problem**: Certain PyTorch operations on CUDA devices use floating-point `atomicAdd` internally, which has non-deterministic accumulation order due to thread race conditions:
  - `torch.Tensor.index_add_`
  - `torch.Tensor.scatter_add_`
  - `torch.bincount`
  - `torch.nn.functional.ctc_loss`
  - `torch.nn.functional.interpolate` with bilinear/bicubic modes.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Rule `R130` (`review` level):
    - Flag direct calls to these operations advising users of known hardware-level nondeterminism and suggesting deterministic alternatives (e.g. `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`).
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/frameworks.py`.

---

title: feat(verify): Audit multi-threading determinism (OMP_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: PyTorch, OpenBLAS, and Intel MKL determinism guides.
- **Problem**: Even with identical seeds, multi-threaded matrix multiplications (via OpenMP, Intel MKL, or OpenBLAS) can yield non-deterministic floating-point roundoff if the number of threads or thread allocation dynamic scheduling varies between runs.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - In `repro-lens verify`:
    - Inspect environment variables: `OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS`, `VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS`.
    - If unpinned or set to dynamic values, emit a warning in the verification report recommending explicit pinning (e.g. `export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` or fixed count).
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/verify.py`.

---

title: feat(notebooks): Detect out-of-order execution risk via notebook execution count gaps (R131)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: Jupyter, `nbdime`, and academic studies on Jupyter reproducibility.
- **Problem**: The single biggest cause of irreproducibility in Jupyter Notebooks (`.ipynb`) is that cells were executed out of order by the human (e.g. Cell 5 executed before Cell 2, or Cell 8 re-executed 3 times). When saved, the notebook reflects the file order, but its outputs reflect the messy human execution sequence.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Rule `R131` (`review` level):
    - In `src/repro_lens/notebooks.py`, inspect cell `execution_count` integers.
    - If `execution_count` sequence is non-monotonic (e.g. `[1, 5, 2, 6]`), contains `null` (unexecuted cells), or jumps unexpectedly, report `R131`: "Notebook cells were executed out of order; rerun from top to bottom before committing."
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/notebooks.py`, `tests/test_notebooks.py`.

---

title: feat(verify): Multi-seed experiment variance & confidence interval verification (--seeds)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: CleanRL and Gymnasium benchmark standards.
- **Problem**: Running an experiment twice with the same seed verifies determinism. But verifying scientific reproducibility across seeds requires testing that metrics don't collapse or swing wildly.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Add `repro-lens verify --seeds 42,43,44,45`:
    - Executes the experiment across $N$ seeds.
    - Computes mean, variance, and standard deviation for each metric.
    - Checks that metric variance remains within configured bounds:
      ```toml
      [tool.repro-lens.verify.stability]
      accuracy = { max_std = 0.02 }
      ```
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/verify.py`, `src/repro_lens/cli.py`.

---

title: feat(verify): Verify input dataset immutability via SHA256 snapshot hashes
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: DVC (Data Version Control) and Git LFS.
- **Problem**: When `repro-lens verify` runs, or `repro-lens compare` compares two runs, if an underlying input data file was silently modified (or a row appended), the comparison fails even though the code is deterministic.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - In `[tool.repro-lens.verify]`, support hashing inputs:
    ```toml
    [tool.repro-lens.verify]
    inputs = ["data/train.csv", "config.yaml"]
    hash-inputs = true
    ```
  - Store SHA256 hashes of all input files in the run report.
  - In `compare`, immediately detect if an input data file changed.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/verify.py`, `src/repro_lens/comparison.py`.

---

title: feat(verify): Add containerized/isolated replay mode via Docker/Podman (--sandbox)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: SWE-bench execution harness & OpenHands sandbox.
- **Problem**: `repro-lens verify` currently runs the experiment directly on the host machine. If an untrusted script or PR modifies files, downloads packages, or writes to global directories, it can pollute the host.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Add `repro-lens verify --sandbox docker`:
    - Automatically mounts the project directory in a clean container, runs verification, and extracts `result.json`.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/verify.py`, `src/repro_lens/cli.py`.

---

title: feat(agent): Generate machine-readable agent review verdicts for AI assistants (agent-eval)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: SWE-bench, Aider, and Antigravity Agent skills.
- **Problem**: AI coding assistants (like Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity) need an immediate, structured verdict after making a refactor: "Did I break reproducibility? If so, what changed?"
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Add `repro-lens agent-review --baseline <before.json> --after <after.json>`:
    - Outputs a specialized JSON format containing:
      - `verdict`: `"APPROVED"` | `"REJECTED"` | `"NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW"`
      - `delta_metrics`: percentage change per metric.
      - `risk_assessment`: explanation of any new unseeded calls introduced in the diff.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/comparison.py`, `skills/reproducibility/`.

---

title: feat(export): Export verification & compare evidence as W&B / MLflow run artifacts
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: Weights & Biases (W&B) and MLflow tracking.
- **Problem**: ML teams track their experiments on W&B or MLflow. Having reproducibility reports stored alongside the run enables teams to audit models before deployment.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Add `--export wandb` or `--export mlflow`:
    - Automatically logs `repro_lens_report.json`, static scan summary, and artifact hashes to the active W&B or MLflow run.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/cli.py`, `src/repro_lens/verify.py`.

title: feat(engine): Custom YAML-based rule definitions (plugin architecture)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: Semgrep custom rules & ESLint plugin architecture.
- **Problem**: Organizations often have internal libraries (e.g. `company_ml.data.load()`) that require specific random seeds. Hardcoding them into ReproLens core is not scalable.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Allow defining custom AST matchers in `.repro-lens/rules.yaml`:
    ```yaml
    rules:
      - id: C101
        severity: warning
        message: "company_ml.split requires explicit seed argument"
        match:
          call: "company_ml.split"
          missing_kwargs: ["seed"]
    ```
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/analysis.py`, `src/repro_lens/project.py`.

---

title: feat(lsp): Implement lightweight Language Server Protocol (LSP) for editor diagnostics
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: Ruff LSP (`ruff-lsp`) and Biome.
- **Problem**: Developers want real-time feedback inside VS Code, Cursor, and Neovim as they write code, rather than waiting for git pre-commit hooks.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Add a lightweight `repro-lens lsp` server command using stdlib / minimal JSON-RPC.
  - Publishes `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` on file save/open.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/lsp.py`, `src/repro_lens/cli.py`.

---

title: feat(cli): Add --add-ignores flag to batch-suppress legacy warnings with comments
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: ESLint (`--fix`), Ruff suppressions.
- **Problem**: When introducing ReproLens to a legacy codebase with 200 findings, manually writing `# repro-lens: ignore[R101] -- Legacy unseeded call` on 200 lines takes hours.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Add `repro-lens check --add-ignores`:
    - Automatically appends `# repro-lens: ignore[CODE] -- TODO: Review reproducibility` to every flagged line.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/cli.py`, `src/repro_lens/project.py`.

---

title: feat(fix): Concrete Syntax Tree (CST) based lossless autofixes for missing seeds
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: LibCST, Ruff autofix engine, ast-grep.
- **Problem**: Python's standard `ast` does not preserve comments or exact token whitespace. To implement safe autofixes (`repro-lens check --fix`), a lossless CST or token-based insertion engine is required.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Use Python's stdlib `tokenize` to find the exact closing parenthesis of a call site and safely inject `, random_state=42` without mangling existing comments.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/autofix.py`, `src/repro_lens/cli.py`.

---

title: feat(analysis): Intra-procedural taint tracking for unseeded RNG parameters
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: CodeQL and SonarQube taint analysis.
- **Problem**: When a developer wraps an estimator:
  ```python
  def make_model(seed=None):
      return RandomForestClassifier(random_state=seed)
  ```
  ReproLens currently sees `random_state=seed` and assumes it is seeded, even though the default argument is `None`!
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Track function parameters within the same file: if a parameter defaults to `None` and is forwarded directly to `random_state`, flag the function definition or the unseeded call site.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/analysis.py`.

---

title: feat(policy): Verify lockfile synchronicity with active environment before verify (P204)
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: `uv lock --check`, `pip check`.
- **Problem**: A user runs `repro-lens verify`, but their local `.venv` has different package versions than what is committed in `uv.lock`. This produces a false sense of reproducibility.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Add policy rule `P204` (`error` level):
    - Check if `uv.lock` or `poetry.lock` exists.
    - If `uv` is available, run `uv lock --check` or compare installed package hashes with lockfile entries.
- **Files**: `src/repro_lens/project.py`, `src/repro_lens/verify.py`.

---

title: feat(ci): GitHub Action check-run summary with collapsible failure diffs
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: GitHub Super-Linter, Vitest PR reporter.
- **Problem**: In GitHub Actions, when `repro-lens verify` or `compare` fails, developers have to dig through raw console logs to find which metric diverged.
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Use GitHub Actions Step Summary (`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`) to write a beautiful markdown table with collapsible diff sections (`<details><summary>Output differences</summary>`).
- **Files**: `action.yml`, `src/repro_lens/project.py`.

title: docs(examples): Reproducible DeepSpeed & Megatron-LM distributed training tutorial
body:
- **SOTA Inspiration**: DeepSpeed / Megatron-LM documentation.
- **Problem**: Contributors and users working on large models need an end-to-end tutorial showing how to achieve bitwise reproducibility across 3D parallelism (Data, Tensor, Pipeline parallel).
- **Proposed Specification**:
  - Add `examples/deepspeed_megatron_review/`:
    - Shows how to configure DeepSpeed MoE / Megatron RNG trackers.
    - Documents why tensor parallel rank seeds must differ while data parallel rank seeds must match.
- **Files**: `examples/deepspeed_megatron_review/README.md`.
